subject: ela
intro: Read each passage carefully, then choose the single best answer. These questions ask you to identify the theme of a text, distinguish a theme from a topic, find the details that convey a theme, and select an accurate, objective summary.

items.prompt:
Read the fable, then answer the question.

A crow was dying of thirst. He found a pitcher with a little water at the bottom, but his beak could not reach it. He almost gave up. Then he noticed pebbles nearby. One by one, he dropped them into the pitcher. Slowly the water rose, until at last the crow could drink. "Bit by bit," he said, "a small effort, repeated, does what one big push cannot."

Which statement best expresses the theme of the passage?
A) Crows are clever birds that live near water.
B) Steady, patient effort can solve a problem that seems impossible at first.
C) A crow found a pitcher and dropped pebbles into it until he could drink.
D) Thirst is dangerous for animals in the wild.
items.answer: B) Steady, patient effort can solve a problem that seems impossible at first.

steps: A theme is a broad lesson about life, not a one-word topic or a retelling of events.
The crow solves his problem by adding one pebble at a time, and his closing words point directly to the lesson, so B states that life lesson.
A is a fact about crows, not a lesson the story teaches. C just restates the plot (what happened) rather than the message. D names a topic or danger but is not the lesson the events convey.
The single best answer is B.
solution.answer: B) Steady, patient effort can solve a problem that seems impossible at first.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Leo was proud of being the fastest runner in class, and he laughed when slow, careful Dana entered the race. Sure that he would win easily, Leo stopped halfway to rest and joke with friends. Dana never stopped. She kept a steady pace the whole way and crossed the finish line first while Leo was still catching his breath.

Which option states a theme of the passage rather than just a topic?
A) Competition
B) Running races
C) Steady, consistent effort can beat raw talent that grows careless.
D) Friendship
items.answer: C) Steady, consistent effort can beat raw talent that grows careless.

steps: A topic is a one-word subject. A theme is a full message about life expressed in a sentence.
Option C is a complete statement of a life lesson that the events of the race teach, so it is the theme.
A (Competition), B (Running races), and D (Friendship) are topics or subjects, not messages about life. Choosing one of these confuses the topic with the theme.
The single best answer is C.
solution.answer: C) Steady, consistent effort can beat raw talent that grows careless.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Mrs. Park baked extra bread every Friday. She wrapped warm loaves and left them on the doorsteps of neighbors who lived alone. She never signed a note or knocked. "A kind act," she told her grandson, "means more when no one is watching for thanks."

Which sentence is the best objective summary of the passage?
A) Mrs. Park is the nicest person in the whole neighborhood, and everyone should be like her.
B) Each Friday Mrs. Park baked extra bread and left warm loaves anonymously on the doorsteps of neighbors who lived alone.
C) Mrs. Park baked bread because she felt lonely and wanted attention from her neighbors.
D) Mrs. Park told her grandson a wise saying about kindness.
items.answer: B) Each Friday Mrs. Park baked extra bread and left warm loaves anonymously on the doorsteps of neighbors who lived alone.

steps: An objective summary reports the key events in order without opinions and without adding or omitting facts.
Option B states what happens (the baking, the warm loaves, the anonymous delivery to neighbors who live alone) with no opinion and no invented detail.

A inserts a personal judgment ('the nicest person,' 'everyone should be like her'). C adds a motive the text never states and that contradicts it. D captures only one line and leaves out the main events, so it is incomplete.
The single best answer is B.
solution.answer: B) Each Friday Mrs. Park baked extra bread and left warm loaves anonymously on the doorsteps of neighbors who lived alone.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

For weeks Maya had bragged that she alone had built the winning science model. The truth was that her partner, Ben, had done most of the wiring while she watched. When the teacher praised the project and asked Maya to explain the circuit, she froze. She did not understand how it worked. Cheeks burning, she finally admitted, "Ben figured out the wiring. I should have said so from the start." The teacher nodded. Later, Ben said the apology meant more to him than any award.

Which statement best expresses the theme of the passage?
A) Taking credit you have not earned eventually leaves you exposed, and honesty repairs what pride breaks.
B) Maya should not have lied about building the science model by herself.
C) Science projects
D) Maya bragged about a model, froze when questioned, then admitted Ben did the wiring.
items.answer: A) Taking credit you have not earned eventually leaves you exposed, and honesty repairs what pride breaks.

steps: The theme is the broad, generalizable lesson the whole passage teaches about life.
Maya's false claim leaves her unable to explain the work, and her honest apology restores her relationship with Ben, so A captures both halves of that lesson and applies beyond this one story.
B is too narrow because it is advice about Maya only, not a message about people in general. C is a topic, not a theme. D restates the plot rather than stating its meaning.
The single best answer is A.
solution.answer: A) Taking credit you have not earned eventually leaves you exposed, and honesty repairs what pride breaks.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

The new student, Priya, sat alone at lunch for a week. Most kids ignored her, but Tomas noticed her sketchbook full of drawings. One day he sat down and asked about them. He did not know anyone else was watching. By the next week, three more students had joined their table, drawn by Tomas's example. Priya, who had thought she would never fit in, finally laughed at lunch.

The theme of this passage is that one person's small act of kindness can change how others behave. Which detail in the passage best conveys this theme?
A) The new student's name is Priya and she is good at drawing.
B) Priya had thought she would never fit in at the new school.
C) Tomas sat down and asked Priya about her drawings, and his example led three more students to join the table.
D) Most of the kids ignored Priya during her first week.
items.answer: C) Tomas sat down and asked Priya about her drawings, and his example led three more students to join the table.

steps: The question gives the theme and asks which detail best conveys it: kindness from one person changing others.
Option C names the decisive action (Tomas sitting down) and its ripple effect (others following his example), which directly develops the stated theme.

A is background information about Priya, not the cause of change. B is her feeling, not the act of kindness. D describes the opposite behavior, what people did before the kindness, so it does not convey the theme.
The single best answer is C.
solution.answer: C) Tomas sat down and asked Priya about her drawings, and his example led three more students to join the table.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

When the river flooded, the Ortega family lost their garden. Carlos, the youngest, had spent all spring growing pumpkins for the fall fair, and now they were gone. He sat by the muddy patch, refusing to speak. His grandmother knelt beside him and pressed a handful of seeds into his palm. "Soil that floods," she said, "is the richest soil of all. Next year your pumpkins will be the biggest in the county." Slowly, Carlos closed his fingers around the seeds and stood up.

Which of the following is the best objective summary of the passage?
A) After a flood destroyed Carlos's pumpkins, his grandmother gave him seeds and encouraged him about next year, and he chose to keep going.
B) Carlos was a foolish boy who cried too much over some lost pumpkins that did not really matter.
C) The Ortega family lost everything they owned in a terrible flood and had to move away from the county.
D) Carlos's grandmother told him that flooded soil is the richest soil of all.
items.answer: A) After a flood destroyed Carlos's pumpkins, his grandmother gave him seeds and encouraged him about next year, and he chose to keep going.

steps: An objective summary covers the key events in order, with no opinion and no facts added or dropped.
Option A reports the flood, the lost pumpkins, the grandmother's seeds and encouragement, and Carlos's choice to continue, all accurately and without judgment.

B inserts opinions ('foolish boy,' 'cried too much'). C adds details the text never states ('lost everything,' 'had to move away'), making it inaccurate. D captures only one quotation and omits the main events.
The single best answer is A.
solution.answer: A) After a flood destroyed Carlos's pumpkins, his grandmother gave him seeds and encouraged him about next year, and he chose to keep going.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

For years Jonah had measured himself against his older brother, Eli, who seemed to win at everything. When Eli left for college, Jonah expected to feel free at last. Instead the house felt larger and quieter than he had imagined. He found himself reading the books Eli had left behind, not to beat him this time, but because he was curious. One evening he caught himself laughing at a note Eli had scribbled in a margin, and he realized he missed his brother. The rivalry, he understood, had been a strange kind of closeness. What he had called competition was partly the only way he had known how to stay near someone he admired.

Which statement most fully captures the central idea of the passage?
A) Jonah was jealous of Eli and was glad when his brother finally left for college.
B) Sibling rivalry is harmful and brothers should never compete with each other.
C) What looks like competition can be a hidden form of closeness, and distance can reveal how much we valued someone.
D) Jonah read his brother's books and laughed at a note Eli had written in the margin.
items.answer: C) What looks like competition can be a hidden form of closeness, and distance can reveal how much we valued someone.

steps: A central idea must account for the whole passage, including Jonah's change in understanding by the end.
Option C captures both the realization that the rivalry was a form of closeness and the way Eli's absence reveals how much Jonah valued him, which is exactly the shift the passage builds to.

A contradicts the ending, where Jonah misses Eli rather than feeling glad. B is an unsupported moral the text never argues. D restates a single event and ignores the realization the passage centers on.
The single best answer is C.
solution.answer: C) What looks like competition can be a hidden form of closeness, and distance can reveal how much we valued someone.

items.prompt:
Read the passage and the draft summary, then answer the question.

Passage: The lighthouse keeper, old Mr. Finch, had warned the village that the storm would be the worst in years. Few listened. When the waves came, it was Finch who rang the bell through the night and guided three fishing boats safely to the harbor, soaked and exhausted by dawn. The next morning the same villagers who had ignored him lined up to shake his hand. Finch only shrugged and went back to trimming the lamp, as if saving them had been nothing unusual.

Draft summary: Mr. Finch warned the village about a dangerous storm. When it struck, this brave and humble hero rang the bell all night and guided three fishing boats safely to harbor. The next morning the grateful villagers thanked him, and he returned to his work.

Which part of the draft summary is a personal opinion rather than an objective statement of what happened?
A) "Mr. Finch warned the village about a dangerous storm."
B) "this brave and humble hero"
C) "he guided three fishing boats safely to harbor"
D) "he returned to his work"

steps: An objective summary states what happened without inserting the writer's judgments or praise.
The phrase 'this brave and humble hero' labels Finch with the writer's opinion of him rather than reporting an event, so B is the opinion.
A, C, and D each report actions that actually occur in the passage (the warning, guiding the boats, returning to work) and contain no judgment.
The single best answer is B.
